passages.note: Lucas voted Yea on adoption of the conference committee report, the final action on the bill's text, and the 30 Nay votes are well above the near-unanimous threshold.
The Indiana General Assembly bill page lists Lucas as a co-author of the enrolled bill.

passages.provision_quote: under state or federal law is not required to obtain or possess a license or permit from the state to carry a handgun in Indiana.
passages.note: The enrolled act rewrites IC 35-47-2-3 so that an adult not otherwise prohibited needs no state license to carry a handgun, and repeals IC 35-47-2-2, IC 35-47-2-2.1 and IC 35-47-2-24 along with the offense of carrying a handgun without a license.

rows.reasoning: Lucas co-authored HB 1296 (2022) and voted Yea on adopting its conference committee report (Yea 69 Nay 30), and the enrolled act provides that a person at least eighteen years of age and not otherwise prohibited "under state or federal law is not required to obtain or possess a license or permit from the state to carry a handgun in Indiana.", while repealing IC 35-47-2-2, IC 35-47-2-2.1 and IC 35-47-2-24 and striking the offense of carrying a handgun without a license. That is the rung reading "Repeal major gun restrictions and let adults carry a firearm without a permit": the instrument repeals the state's handgun carry licensing regime and lets adults carry without a permit. It excludes the rung that would "Add no new restrictions, and at most loosen rules on carrying, such as honoring permits across state lines", because abolishing the permit requirement goes past that rung's "at most".
